title: Crypto misuse: wolfssl CBC update() permits encryption with zero IV
description: In wolfssl_aes_cbc.c, wolfssl_aes_cbc_update() performs CBC encryption/decryption without checking whether set_iv() or gen_iv() was called first. The session context has no ivlen or iv_set field to track IV state. wc_AesSetKey() is called in sess_init with IV=NULL, which installs a zero IV in the wolfCrypt Aes struct. A caller who skips SET_IV/GEN_IV and calls UPDATE directly will encrypt with IV=0, a weak deterministic IV. Contrast: wolfssl_aes_gcm_update() correctly checks ctx->ivlen == 0 and returns -EINVAL; kcapi_skcipher_update() checks ctx->ivlen == 0 and returns -EINVAL. Fix: add ivlen tracking field to wolfssl_aes_cbc_ctx and check it in update() (check 2d).
